precepts.text: O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that liveth at rest in his possessions. The fear of death is often the fear of leaving things behind. In this truth you cannot get attached to things; the saints love not their lives unto death.
precepts.point: No man can serve two masters; ye cannot serve God and mammon. Mammon is money. The elite want nothing to do with God because they think they are in their heaven already.

note.label: Covetous Eyes Will Be Put Out

precepts.why:
“Ye cannot serve God and mammon.” Mammon is money. That is why the elite do not want to hear anything about God: they feel like they are in their heaven already. And that is why a lot of people are scared of dying. Many times the fear of death is not death itself.

“O death, how bitter is the remembrance of thee to a man that liveth at rest in his possessions”. That man is living so good that the moment he thinks of death, he says, I have to leave all this behind? Because of his possessions his mind is on here. He is not thinking about the possession over there, what the Most High has in store for us that eyes have not seen and ears have not heard. He wants it now.

“Unto the man that hath nothing to vex him, and that hath prosperity in all things: yea, unto him that is yet able to receive meat!” Do you think a covetous man wants to die, after he just got that nice Porsche and bought that nice house? No. He needs to enjoy it a little more, because it is never enough to a covetous man.

That is why in this truth you cannot get attached to things. The saints love not their lives unto death. Nothing on this planet can hold us back from doing what we are supposed to be doing, and whatever is going to happen to us is what will happen; the apostles were appointed last, unto death. You cannot hold to money and serve God too.

precepts.text: Prepare slaughter for his children for the iniquity of their fathers. That is not what we said; that is what God said.
precepts.point: If the reproach falls on the descendants, they are direct beneficiaries of the evil their forefathers did. That is fact.

precepts.text: Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother.
precepts.point: Christ told a woman of another nation it is not meet to take the children's bread and cast it to dogs, and she said, Truth, Lord; and four-legged dogs did not pierce Christ's hands and feet, for the dogs that compassed him were the other nations, in that case the Romans.

note.label: Deuteronomy 23: Who May Enter the Congregation and the Holy Camp

precepts.why:
“There shall be no whore of the daughters of Israel, nor a sodomite of the sons of Israel.” A sodomite is the biblical word for a homosexual, and the whore of the daughters of Israel here is the same sin in the daughters, what we today would call lesbians.

Ecclesiasticus: “Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man”. Whoredom is a thing to be ashamed of before father and mother.

There is a heavy push in the world today for our men to be homosexuals and our sisters to be lesbians; popular entertainers are used to influence the younger generation to sin, just as young rappers were dressed in skirts and dresses until it became cool to be gay. This is what we have to bring our people back from: by being an example, the men being an example, the sisters being an example in the way they dress and carry themselves.

precepts.text: Born to a curse and dying with a curse for a portion; and the more we have increased as a people, the worse it has become.
precepts.point: Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: we are born under the curses and we die still living under them.

note.label: Deuteronomy 28: The Blessings and the Curses That Identify Israel

precepts.why:
“Cursed shalt thou be when thou comest in, and cursed shalt thou be when thou goest out.” He is talking about Jerusalem, coming in and going out of the city, but it is twofold: it is coming in and going out of life itself.

Ecclesiasticus, for you newer people in the Apocrypha, spells it out: “Woe be unto you, ungodly men, which have forsaken the law of the most high God! for if ye increase, it shall be to your destruction: And if ye be born, ye shall be born to a curse: and if ye die, a curse shall be your portion.” We are born under the curses, coming in, and we die still living under them, going out; a curse is our portion. And the more we have increased as a people, the worse it has become, because “if ye increase, it shall be to your destruction”. All of it for forsaking the law of the most high God.

precepts.text: Be ashamed of whoredom is the point set against the attire of the harlot.
precepts.point: So she caught him and kissed him, and with an impudent face said she had peace offerings and had paid her vows. This is the opposite of the modest apparel the sisters are taught.

note.label: Proverbs 7: The Adulteress Hunts for the Precious Soul

precepts.why:
“And, behold, there met him a woman with the attire of an harlot, and subtil of heart.” She is loud and stubborn, out in the streets, lying in wait at every corner, and “with an impudent face” she catches him and kisses him. There is no shame in her.

Ecclesiasticus says where the shame belongs: “Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man”. Be ashamed of whoredom. That is the point set against the attire of the harlot: the modest woman is ashamed of whoredom before her father and mother, and the woman of Proverbs 7 wears it in the street with an impudent face.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
Job is the precept that there is no inquisition in the grave. Job was catching so much hell that he said “Why died I not from the womb? why did I not give up the ghost when I came out of the belly?” Why didn’t I die as a baby? His kids got put to death, he lost all his businesses, he got sick, all kinds of plagues were on his flesh, and his wife was a nag getting on his nerves.

“Why did the knees prevent me? or why the breasts that I should suck?” The knees are the mother rocking a baby on her knees to keep it up and about. “For now should I have lain still and been quiet, I should have slept: then had I been at rest”, “with kings and counsellors of the earth”, “or with princes that had gold, who filled their houses with silver”, “or as an hidden untimely birth”: a still birth, “as infants which never saw light.”

“There the wicked cease from troubling; and there the weary be at rest. There the prisoners rest together; they hear not the voice of the oppressor.” The prisoners are our people, at rest together in death. “The small and great are there”, in the grave, at rest, “and the servant is free from his master.”

So when we die, brothers and sisters, we are all at rest, whether you are righteous or you are wicked as hell.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
“The righteous perisheth, and no man layeth it to heart”, and Isaiah says “the righteous is taken away from the evil to come.” When he dies “He shall enter into peace: they shall rest in their beds”: the chambers of rest.

Then: “each one walking in his uprightness.” When the righteous die they are walking in their uprightness, walking before the Lord. They are not really dead. The wicked are at rest, they sleep, but the righteous are up, talking before the Lord.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

precepts.why:
This shows the righteous more. At the fifth seal John saw “under the altar the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held.” Remember, they are dead, yet “they cried with a loud voice, saying, How long, O Lord, holy and true, dost thou not judge and avenge our blood on them that dwell on the earth?”

So not only are they walking, they are talking to the Lord, asking for vengeance. We have to get that in our minds and understand what death is and what it is not.

“Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before thee, and that come after; for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.” Death is a sentence on all flesh. Everyone before us died, and everyone after us will.

So when Hebrews says Christ delivers them “who through fear of death were all their lifetime subject to bondage”, it cannot be the regular death, because that sentence is still on all flesh, believers too. The death Christ delivers us from is the eternal death, the condemnation.

note.label: LEARNING TO SEE WITH SPIRITUAL EYES | Psalm 23

precepts.why: “And if ye be born, ye shall be born to a curse”: you don’t know who you are, you don’t know what your purpose in life is. “And if ye die, a curse shall be your portion”: if you grow old and die, you still won’t know who you are or what your purpose was upon the earth. You still fall under God’s curses, cursed coming in and cursed going out.

note.label: Unlocking The Three Angels Prophecies And More

precepts.why:
“The inheritance of sinners’ children shall perish”. This is the man that steals lands and property, homes and houses, and then passes it down to his children. “And their posterity shall have a perpetual reproach”: they’re always going to have a reproach.

“The children will complain of an ungodly father”: it wasn’t me, it was my forefathers; we didn’t enslave you, it was my fathers. “Because they shall be reproached for his sake.” We all say it to them today, and they say it wasn’t me, it was my father, I just benefit from it. Yeah, you. That’s what’s going on now: no accountability, zero responsibility, and an enormous amount of self-entitlement.

points: The inheritance of sinners' children shall perish and their posterity shall have a perpetual reproach.
My children keep discipline: where do they learn that discipline from? From the parents. How are they going to keep it if you leave them to their lonesome?

note.label: The Writings on The Wall Radio, Part 2

points: The children of sinners are abominable children. Why? Because the children of sinners learn the ways of their father, and they become conversant in the dwelling of the ungodly.

This is an example to us now as fathers: do not be a sinner, do not teach our children sin, because you make it hard for them. Yes, repentance is open unto them, but they have got an uphill climb because of the climate that you as a father established for them. This is why it's not good to sleep around, why it's good for marriage, why it's good to learn God's commandments and apply them, so that you can do the best by your children.

The children will complain of an ungodly father, because they shall be reproached for his sake. Now your children have an uphill climb because of the evil you perpetuated and taught them; now they have got to break all these generational curses, break through all that trauma. Don't put your children in that position.
But if you grew up like that, if your father was ungodly, if you have been reproached for his sake, God says there is still a way of repentance. You can now repent.

“Fear not the sentence of death, remember them that have been before thee, and that come after; for this is the sentence of the Lord over all flesh.” Death is the sentence from the Lord over all flesh. Everybody is destined to die; this physical body is destined to perish.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “And why art thou against the pleasure of the most High?” That is heavy. “There is no inquisition in the grave”: when you die there is no inquisition, no questioning, “whether thou have lived ten, or an hundred, or a thousand years.” When we die, we are at rest.

note.label: The Keys Of Hell & Death: The Lake Of Fire

points: “Be ashamed of whoredom before father and mother: and of a lie before a prince and a mighty man”: the Bible says to be ashamed of that. In the Apocrypha, where it lists the things to be ashamed of. In some things you can be shamefaced, but in these things you must be ashamed.

“Of an offence before a judge and ruler; of iniquity before a congregation and people; of unjust dealing before thy partner and friend”: and of theft in regard of the place where thou sojournest, and in regard of the truth of God and his covenant. And to lean with thine elbow upon the meat, and of scorning to give and take, and of silence before them that salute thee.
